title: Personal KPI check-in - Sophia Martinez - week of 2026-03-02
content:
Quick personal check-in + scratchpad for weekly KPIs, blockers, and next steps. Informal - notes to self and things to bring up in 1:1/weekly sync.

OKRs (Q1 2026) - my focus areas
- O1: Improve serving latency and tail performance for common models
  - KR1: Reduce p95 latency for text-generation (up to 2k tokens) from 420ms -> 320ms across hosted pool (measured on canary)
  - KR2: Identify top 3 kernel hotspots and land optimizations or fallback paths
- O2: Reduce per-token infra cost for mid-sized prompts for Redwood Dedicated customers
  - KR1: Experiment + validate 4-bit quant/kv-cache mix; target -15% cost
- O3: Dev experience: reduce mean time to reproduce perf regressions for customers by 30%

This week (what I actually did)
- Ran distributed profiling on canary for gen-7b variant (see JIRA-5678) - found two hot loops in kv-cache serialization (lines flagged in profiler output).
- POC patch for serialization (PR #234) landed on branch; microbench shows ~8% reduction in serialize time. Need reviewer feedback from Priya.
- Setup synthetic workload to simulate 95th percentile sequences; found p95 still spikes when batch size > 8 and seq_len > 1k. Hypothesis: batching + attention kernel mismatch.
- Wrote draft notes for Confluence (CON-1234) about prefix cache architecture and known tradeoffs - link above.

Metrics snapshot (rough, from canary telemetry)
- p50: 180ms (stable)
- p95: 395ms (was 420ms last week)
- tokens/s per GPU (small model): 1.2k -> 1.25k (after micro-optimizations)
- Cost per 1M tokens (hosted canary): $8.75 (baseline $10 target for Dedicated experiments)

Accomplishments
- Lightweight serializer refactor implemented and benchmarked locally (+8% on serialize path).
- Confluence doc started to centralize prefix cache decisions - useful for onboarding new SREs/SEs.
- Repro harness extended to cover long-seq scenarios (seq 2k) - caught a regression earlier this week.

Blockers / open questions
- Need Priya + Jordan to review PR #234 - we should avoid any change that regresses memory usage for small prompts.
- KV-cache serialization optimization looks promising but may interact poorly with multi-tenant cache eviction policy (need SRE input).
- Can we get increased canary capacity for 3 days next week to run sustained experiments? Currently throttled at peak hours. Who owns canary pool scaling? (cc @platform-eng)

Next week goals (concrete)
- Get PR #234 reviewed and landed (blocker: reviewer bandwidth).
- Run A/B on canary with serializer change + baseline for 48h traffic window (overnight runs to capture tail).
- Instrument memory metrics per-request (add counters) to watch for regressions in small-prompt cases.
- Draft experiment plan for 4-bit quant + kv-cache mix in Dedicated; sync with Product (Priya) by Wed.

Action items (TODOs)
- [ ] Ping Priya for PR review (in Slack) - target: Mon AM.
- [ ] Create canary scaling request ticket (JIRA-5791) - assign to platform-eng.
- [ ] Add per-request memory counters (quick patch) - estimate 1 day.
- [ ] Consolidate CON-1234 into 'prefix-cache-playbook' and link to runbook.

1:1 notes for manager (to bring up)
- Progress on p95 improvements - small wins but still above target; need cross-team help for kernel-level changes.
- Resource ask: short canary expansion for controlled experiments (explain cost-benefit).
- Career note: interested in leading the Dedicated cost-optimization project if PM bandwidth is available.

Reflections / personal
- Felt productive mid-week when tests reproduced the spike - having deterministic reproducer = huge multiplier.
- Need to be more proactive about blocking reviewers; set aside review hours in calendar?
- Keep checklist handy for regression rollout (automated safety gates, automatic fallback to baseline).

Misc scratch notes (todo later)
- Try 'small-batch + chunked-attn' combination on local gpu1 for quick signal.
- Follow up with infra on observability retention (token-level traces) - costs are higher but useful for debugging.
- Draft short blurb for team sync about what the prefix cache does (one slide).

End of note. Revisit next Thurs morning to update metrics and progress.
